question: Q-009
reason: Read test/arch/rules.ts lines 213 to 270: the only loop is over Object.entries(modules); PINNED_EGRESS is read as PINNED_EGRESS[name] inside that loop, so a pinned module absent from the graph yields no violation. The spec scenario at specs/architecture-rules/spec.md line 24 requires each fixture result to carry egress-pin violations, and design.md decision 6 pins the egress modules to exactly three names. The existing test only removes the egress property while keeping the gateway row, so it cannot detect the gap. The finding stands and matches the earlier Q-002 rejection.

checked.claim: The integrity check only visits rows that exist in the given graph.
The pin is consulted only for the row being visited, never for a pinned name absent from the graph.
The missing-egress branch fires only when the pinned row exists, so a deleted gateway row is not reported.
The shipped test keeps the gateway row and only drops its egress property, so it cannot detect the missing-row gap.

checked.quote: each result also carries the egress-pin violations (these fixtures name no egress module), so the test asserts with `some`, not on the length
checked.claim: The specification requires fixtures without egress modules to produce egress-pin violations.

checked.quote: the modules with an `egress` value are exactly `observability`, `identity` and `gateway` (a pin: a new capability needs a reviewed rule edit)
checked.claim: Design decision 6 pins the set of egress modules exactly, which a graph lacking one of them violates.

question: Q-010
reason: Read test/arch/sources.ts: namedBindingsAreTypeOnly checks node.isTypeOnly, then node.namedBindings for an ImportClause, and returns true when all named elements are type-only; it never inspects the default name, so a mixed default-plus-type-named import is typeOnly. Read test/arch/rules.ts: checkNetwork continues past any ref with typeOnly true before the worker_threads and network checks. Design decision 3 restricts the all-type rule to declarations with only named specifiers, so the behaviour contradicts the design and bypasses the network rule.

checked.claim: This helper decides whether an import or export declaration is type-only.
For an import clause only the named bindings are inspected, never the default binding name.
The result is true whenever every named element is type-modified, regardless of a default value binding.
collectImports uses that helper to set typeOnly on import declarations.
checkNetwork skips every ref marked typeOnly, so the mixed import of node:https is not reported.

checked.quote: `typeOnly` is true for `import type`, `export type ... from`, an import type node, and a declaration with only named specifiers, at least one, all `type`-modified.
checked.claim: The design treats a declaration as type-only by named specifiers only when it has nothing but named specifiers, so a default binding makes it a value import.
